Starting school at Lenham - a parents guide

pageCache.text:
Welcome to Lenham Primary School
We are a good school, with a family feel, which is made up of pupils and staff who take PRIDE in everything they do. Inclusion runs through the heart of the school. In the pursuit of ‘Personal Excellence’, pupils uphold the highest expectations of their own and their classmates’ behaviour. They are incredibly kind and considerate of others, making the school a warm and nurturing place to be. If you wish to contact us, please go to the 'Welcome' tab.
01622 858260

Illness, Absence and Holiday
Like all state schools, we are required to keep records of attendance for every pupil. We expect children to be in every day that the school is open. Absence is only authorised for health reasons including medical appointments.
Absence is not authorised for any term-time holidays as per the Department of Education Regulations 2013. Penalty Notices of £160 will be issued to each parent for each child reduced to £80 if paid within 21 days. Please see our online Attendance Policy for further information. An attendance record for every child is included in his or her Annual Report. The statistics are also included in national records and our School Profile.
If your child will be absent, due to ill health, please contact the school office on 01622 858260 to advise, on each day of the illness, before 9am.

pageCache.text:
Breakfast Club
Breakfast club runs every day from 7.45 am until the start of school. Places are strictly limited and MUST be pre-booked with the office. The cost of breakfast club is £4.50 which includes food. A selection of breakfast options are available every day, with cereals, toast, fruit, yoghurt and daily specials including crumpets, pancakes and brioche. Milk or water are provided to drink.
Fees MUST be paid in advance by Parent Pay or Pay Point. We do accept Childcare vouchers but if you intend to use this method please contact the office. If you are approved to pay via Childcare vouchers, and have made a payment please email the office detailing how you would like the funds attributed.
Unfortunately we are unable to offer a refund if your child does not attend a session as we would have already arranged staff cover (unless the cancellation is made in writing by 9am Friday of the preceding week).

Music at Lenham Primary
Music is planned in-line with the statements laid out in the National Curriculum. Cross-curricular links are made where possible using Cornerstones, with Kapow being used to supplement and provide extra support and resources to enhance music teaching.
What have you learnt in Music this year?
I have played on a glockenspiel, drums and an ocarina.
I liked using the app on the Chromebook to make my own music.
I love creating my own music

Children starting in September 2022
Please contact the School to book your guided tour. This will be a chance for you and your child to receive a tour and to find out about everything that happens at Lenham Primary School. You will also have a chance to speak to the admissions team and senior members of staff.
Admission ProcessTo apply for a firm place at a Primary School for your child for September 2022, you will need to complete a special form called a Common Application Form (RCAF form for short). The application process finishes on Tuesday 15th January 2022. We strongly recommend that you apply online at www.kent.gov.uk/ola.
If you apply online a paper RCAF must not be submitted and vice versa.
If you applied online you will receive an email from KCC Admissions on 18th March 2022 after 4pm to tell you which school you have been offered. Admissions cannot guarantee the exact time you will receive your email, this depends on your email service provider. You can also log in after 5pm on 18th March 2022 to view your offer online. If you applied by post, Admissions will send your offer by first class post on the same day.
You will then need to inform the school in writing as to whether you will accept the place or not. At this point you will also need to come to school with proof of address as to the only or main residence of your child. This will need to be in the form of each of these documents:
These documents should not be more than three months old and preferably should show that the child was resident at the address at the time of the closing date.
We need to see ALL THREE of these documents for EVERY child being admitted (even those who have siblings at school already). If you are unable to provide the above documents, to prove your child’s only or main residence, the Local Authority has the right to take your child’s place away.If you have any queries about the Admission process please ring or come into school. You can also contact the Kent Admissions Team on 03000 41 21 21 or visit their website
For more information please go to http://www.kent.gov.uk/education-and-children/schools/school-places/primary-school-places

Emailing Parents
At Lenham Primary School we use email to communicate with our parents. We send emails to the email address, linked to each child, held on Bromcom. We email out using Parentpay.
Please make sure you inform the school office should any of your contact details change.
We strive to be as paperless as possible so we use Parentpay to obtain parental consent for school events.
We use School Cloud to support the organisation of parent consultation appointments and, when necessary, as the platform for virtual meetings.

Family Forum
This is a safe environment for the school and parents to work together.
On Tuesday, we held our first Family Forum, with a focus on worries—a common and natural human emotion. We explored how worries, while normal, can sometimes become overwhelming and affect daily life.
Together, we discussed a range of concerns children may have, from fears like being scared of the dark to more complex thoughts such as "What if my parents split up?" Mrs. Grieve introduced the book What to Do When You Worry Too Much, a child-friendly Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT) resource that helps children understand and manage their worries. In school, we regularly use this book in small social groups to support emotional well-being. We also run similar groups using What to Do When You Grumble Too Much (focused on overcoming obstacles) and What to Do When Your Temper Flares (focused on managing anger).
Family Forum Recap – The Importance of Sleep
In our last Family Forum, we explored why sleep is so important and discussed useful strategies to support a good night’s rest.
Tips for a Better Night’s Sleep
Be respectful.
Allow people to speak.
Be supportive.
To help our bodies grow.
To help us stay alert and concentrate.

ParentPay
At Lenham Primary School we operate a 'cashless' office. Any payments are processed through ParentPay. Here you will be able to make payments for Breakfast Club, School Dinners, School Visits and extra curricular experiences (e.g. Bikeability)
If you have any difficulties accessing the service please contact the office who will be happy to help you gain access.

Everyone at this school believes that parents play a very important part in their child’s education. A strong partnership between home and school makes a big difference to the children in our care. From the very beginning, parents are invited to take an active part in school life. There are meetings, newsletters, open days, formal consultations, annual reports and numerous other ways that school and home come together. We have an “open door” policy where parents are always welcome to come in and discuss matters with members of staff.
Parents help in school in many ways. Some volunteer to help in class with learning activities, reading etc. or accompany children on trips.
We have a very active Parent, Teacher Association that does a great deal to improve the life and work of the school. Everyone enjoys the many activities they organise for the children and families and the money raised makes a very big impact on the school.
If you have any questions at all, please feel free to contact a member of the PTA on lenhamprimarypta@gmail.com and we will also be at hand to help.
Up and coming events
What we have achieved so far!
This academic year, our PTA has worked incredibly hard to raise funds for important new resources for our school. We are delighted to share that, thanks to the generous donations from parents and members of our local community, we have successfully achieved our goal of funding 30 new Chromebooks and a new sand pit.
We are extremely proud of what we have accomplished together. However, our work doesn’t stop there. We are committed to making our school environment the best it can possibly be for all our children.
To continue supporting this goal, we still have several exciting events planned:
Thank you to everyone who has supported us so far — whether through donating, volunteering, or attending events. Your continued generosity and enthusiasm make a real difference to our school community.

Please remember if we all sell at affordable low prices then we can also buy at these same low prices! You have an option to donate any proceeds back to the Lenham Primary PTA. Any donations will be gratefully received and help support our efforts for the children.

Severe Weather Plan
Emergency Closure
Extreme Weather Arrangements - All the ways you can find out
There will be an announcement posted as soon as possible after the decision to close the school has been made. However, if the bad weather is widespread, the website may be difficult to access due to the heavy demand at the server. The website may be difficult to access both for us to update and for you to read, but we will do our best.
A list of school closures will be posted on the Kent County Council’s website at kentclosures. Kent radio stations will use this list to broadcast closures.
An e-mail will be sent to you once the decision to close has been made. If you have also signed up to receive emergency text messages, a text message will be sent to the primary mobile phone number listed on your account.

Uniform
We feel that uniform is important as it helps to establish school identity, a smart appearance and helps parents overcome the problems of dressing choosy fashion-conscious children!
The uniform is basically green, gold and grey. Various combinations are possible.
Green ‘Lenham Primary School’ sweatshirt, or bottle green, plain jumpers or cardigans Yellow polo shirt (years R-5)
White polo shirt, blouse or shirt (year 6 only)
Grey trousers or skirt or pinafore dress
White, black or grey socks or tights
Black shoes or fully black trainers – please only buy shoes with laces once your child can tie them.
Wellington boots must be named and kept at school all year, for playing outside on the field when it’s wet, muddy or snowy.
Summer Uniform (optional can be wore Easter till October Half term)
Green or Yellow checked summer dresses
Grey skirts and pinafores may be worn in winter or summer
Hairstyles and Hairbands
No child will be permitted to have a haircut (e.g. tramlines) or coloured in such a way that may cause a distraction to other children. Children with long hair must have it tied back.
Children are permitted to have a simple ‘Alice’ band in black, brown or green. Simple hair clips for keeping hair back are allowed. No other hair decoration is permitted and the children will be asked to remove it should anything be worn to school.
Every child needs to have his/her kit in school every day. Children who do not have their kit are not able to participate.
House T-shirt. You will be advised what house your child will be in. Siblings are placed in the same house.
